title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
text:
Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
[Repository README](../README.md) · [Development setup](setup.md) · [Validation](validation.md) · [Foundation versioning](versioning.md) · [ADR-0014](adr/0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) · [ADR-0017](adr/0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md)
This is the practical reference for turning a revision of Orion into a new, independent project and for keeping that project's foundation current: what to decide and provide, how to run the initialization, what the new repository contains, what to do next, and how provenance and foundation upgrades work. [ADR-0014](adr/0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) records the ancestry and provenance decision; [ADR-0017](adr/0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md) records the clean-baseline contract. The commands exist in every Orion checkout; the canonical Orion repository itself is never initialized as a project.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Model
text:
Model
The canonical `GabriellMDias/Orion` repository is the upstream development foundation. A derived project is an independent Git repository with its own `origin`, branches, pull requests, CI history, human actions, product decisions, and releases. It starts from a clean clone of Orion and keeps Orion's commit history, so Git can compute what changed upstream and merge it later, but its first commit removes Orion's own reference implementation and development history and gives the repository the project's identity.
Concern
Mechanism
Identity and provenance
[`.orion/project.json`](../.orion/project.json), validated by `pnpm orion:check`
Clean-baseline contract
[`.orion/derivation.json`](../.orion/derivation.json): foundation-only paths, project-owned files and their templates, and the foundation workspace package scope
Immutable starting point
`foundation.initializedFromCommit`: the published Orion commit the project was initialized from; never changes
Current foundation
`foundation.baselineCommit`: the newest Orion commit integrated and validated through a reviewed merge
Canonical upstream
Local remote `orion-upstream`: fetch-only (its push URL is disabled), fetches no tags, and is tracked by no local branch
Product repository
Recorded as `repository.url`; each clone's `origin` is that repository or a fork or mirror of it, never the foundation ([remote rules](#remote-rules))
In the Orion repository the manifest has `"kind": "foundation"` and only describes Orion. A derived project's manifest (schema version 2) has `"kind": "project"` and additionally records its npm `packageScope` and its foundation ancestry. The Living Documentation Portal links source files to the manifest's repository.
A derived project inherits [Apache-2.0-licensed Orion source](../LICENSE). The project remains responsible for licensing its independently created product code and for applicable obligations of inherited and third-party material; Orion's license does not choose the project's overall license.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Prerequisites
text:
Prerequisites
Git with `user.name` and `user.email` configured, Node.js 24.13.0, and pnpm 11.25.0.
A running Testcontainers-compatible container runtime: initialization regenerates the database reference from a migrated PostgreSQL.
Playwright Chromium for the browser tests in `pnpm validate` ([setup](setup.md#prepare-a-clean-checkout)).
A fresh, full clone of Orion that contains no other work. Shallow clones cannot preserve Orion's ancestry.
Permission to create the product repository before publishing. Initialization never contacts the product repository: it creates no repositories and pushes nothing.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: What carries over, what is removed, and what is adapted
text:
What carries over, what is removed, and what is adapted
Outcome
Content
Preserved from the foundation
Architecture, principles, policies, accepted ADRs, setup and validation guides, runbook guidance, and this guide; the validation gate, agent instructions, CI workflow, and Renovate configuration; the API runtime (configuration, telemetry, health, error registry, module contract, PostgreSQL client, optional JWT verification); the web shell and Living Documentation Portal; the SDK package; the derivation tooling and contract; Orion's full Git history
Removed as foundation-only
Orion's Approval Request reference implementation: its API feature, Prisma models, migration, metadata, runtime grants, smoke, tests, web module, browser tests and journeys, and domain documentation. Orion's own implementation plan, human actions, and acceptance and release history
Adapted or created for the project
The manifest (`kind: project`, name, package scope, provenance); `README.md`; the API and web composition files, which compose no modules; a neutral brand mark and touch icon; the project's plan and human actions in `docs/project/`; workspace package names, the lockfile, and imports; generated OpenAPI, SDK types, configuration, error, and database references, and portal data; the remotes `origin` and `orion-upstream`
Kept as the foundation's technical namespace
`ORION_*` configuration names, `orion_*` token claims and database role names, the `Orion required gate` check name, the `.orion/` directory, the `orion:*` commands, and the `orion-upstream` remote. Renaming them would touch shared files throughout the repository and conflict on every upgrade; the check name is also referenced by branch protection. Accepted ADRs keep their original wording
The [content ownership](#content-ownership) contract defines these categories precisely and how each behaves during upgrades.

Worktree
Clean; nothing is pushed until you publish
`pnpm validate` passes in this state, including the shell and portal browser journeys.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Next steps after creation
text:
Next steps after creation
The project's [README](../README.md) routes to its plan and human actions, which track these steps with stable IDs.
**Publish and validate (PH-01, PJ-01).** Push `main` to the new repository and confirm that `pnpm validate` passes locally and that the repository's CI runs.
**Protect the repository (PH-02 to PH-04).** Require pull requests and the `Orion required gate` check on `main`, keep merge commits available for foundation upgrades, enable Renovate, and enable the applicable GitHub security controls. Settings verified for Orion do not apply to the new repository.
**Onboard contributors.** Each clone needs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the local configuration from [setup](setup.md). Run `pnpm orion:upstream` and `git fetch orion-upstream` in any clone that will inspect or perform foundation upgrades; clones receive no `orion-upstream` remote automatically.
**Define the product (PH-05, PJ-02).** Record the product scope, actors, first capabilities, data classification, and acceptance criteria, then replace the README introduction and current state.
**Build the first module (PJ-03).** Add its schema, reviewed migration, contract, SDK use, web workflow, tests, and documentation as described for [API modules](../apps/api/README.md#modules) and [web modules](../apps/web/README.md#modules), and compose it in `apps/api/src/modules.ts` and `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`. [Orion's reference implementation](#orions-reference-implementation) shows a complete module.
**Replace the placeholder identity (PJ-04).** Replace the brand mark and regenerate the touch icon as described under [web identity](../apps/web/README.md#identity).
**Decide the product license (PH-06)** before distribution requires it.
**Add conditional work when it becomes real (PJ-05).** An identity provider, durable releases, or a deployment environment become new tasks and human actions in the project's own files.
Keep the project's plan and human actions current as work proceeds; `AGENTS.md` routes contributors and agents to them through the README's Current state.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Orion's reference implementation
text:
Orion's reference implementation
The Orion repository composes a complete Approval Request module that demonstrates the architecture from database to browser and is exercised by Orion's validation gate. It is foundation-only: initialization removes it, and no project-owned or shared file refers to it. To study it while building a module, read it in Orion at the commit recorded as the project's baseline, for example in a separate Orion clone or with `git show <baseline>:<path>` after `git fetch orion-upstream`. The paths it occupies are listed in [`.orion/derivation.json`](../.orion/derivation.json). Copy patterns, not the feature: a product module belongs under its own name and is composed in the project's `modules.ts` and `modules.tsx`.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Provenance and foundation upgrades
text:
Provenance and foundation upgrades
Provenance is what makes upgrades possible. Initialization records the Orion commit in both `foundation.initializedFromCommit`, which never changes, and `foundation.baselineCommit`. Because the project keeps Orion's history, Git can compute what changed upstream since the baseline and merge it with a normal three-way merge. Each upgrade merges a newer Orion commit with its history and then records it as the new baseline; `pnpm orion:check` verifies that the baseline is an ancestor of `HEAD`, and `pnpm orion:status` compares it with a fetched `orion-upstream`. The derivation contract travels with every upgrade, and `pnpm orion:prune` reapplies it, so the project stays free of foundation-only content and keeps its own package scope. [Stable semantic tags](versioning.md) make released foundation points easier to identify: a project may be described as derived from a tagged Orion release when its initialization commit matches that tag, while the manifest continues to record the exact commit SHA.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Inspect provenance
text:
Inspect provenance
pnpm orion:status

It prints the project identity and package scope, the initialization and recorded baseline commits, whether `orion-upstream` is configured and fetch-only, and, after `git fetch orion-upstream`, how many upstream commits follow the baseline and whether integrated commits are not yet recorded. It does not fetch or change anything.
`pnpm orion:check` runs in `pnpm validate`.
In Orion, it validates the manifest and derivation contract, requires every foundation-only path and template to exist, and rejects shared tracked files that link to, import, name, or mention foundation-only content. Derivation tooling, ADRs, this guide, and generated output are exempt.
In a project, it validates the manifest and contract, requires the project plan and human actions and the root package name of the recorded scope, rejects any foundation-only path and any remaining reference to the foundation package scope in code or configuration, requires both recorded commits to exist with the initialization commit an ancestor of the baseline and the baseline an ancestor of `HEAD`, and applies the [remote rules](#remote-rules). It needs full history; CI already uses `fetch-depth: 0`.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Remote rules
text:
Remote rules
Git remotes are local configuration, so other clones of the project do not receive `orion-upstream`. Configure it in any clone with:
pnpm orion:upstream
git fetch orion-upstream

Remote
Rule
Enforced by
`origin`
Must not identify the Orion foundation through its fetch or push URL, so product work never has the foundation as its normal push target. It need not equal the project's `repository.url`: contributors may work through a fork or mirror.
`pnpm orion:upstream` refuses; `pnpm orion:check` fails
`orion-upstream`, when present
Its fetch URL must identify the foundation repository recorded in the manifest.
`pnpm orion:upstream` refuses; `pnpm orion:check` fails
`orion-upstream`, when present
Its only push URL must be the disabled `orion-upstream-is-fetch-only`.
`pnpm orion:check` fails and directs you to rerun `pnpm orion:upstream`
`orion-upstream`, when absent
Valid; a normal clone has no foundation remote until a developer configures it.
—
Local branches
No local branch may track `orion-upstream`; an argument-free `git pull` would otherwise merge foundation changes outside a reviewed upgrade.
`pnpm orion:check` fails and directs you to rerun `pnpm orion:upstream`
`pnpm orion:upstream` adds `orion-upstream` from the manifest when absent, replaces every push URL of it with the disabled one, disables its tags, and removes upstream tracking of it from every local branch. It is safe to rerun.
Repository identities compare as normalized HTTPS URLs, so HTTPS, SSH, and scp-like forms of the same repository match. Host names are case-insensitive, but repository path case is significant because self-hosted servers may treat `acme/Ledger` and `acme/ledger` as different repositories: accepting a URL as a given repository, as for `orion-upstream` or the `origin` checked before initialization, requires the exact path. Refusing a URL because it could reach the foundation, as for `origin` or a new project's repository, ignores path case, because hosts such as GitHub resolve differently cased paths to the same repository. An explicit non-default HTTPS port is part of the identity: `https://git.example.com:8443/acme/ledger` differs from `https://git.example.com/acme/ledger`, while `:443` is the same endpoint as no port. A non-default SSH port only selects the SSH transport and does not identify the HTTPS endpoint, so such a URL is refused as a project repository and never matches the foundation; supply the repository's HTTPS URL instead.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Upgrade to a newer Orion revision
text:
Upgrade to a newer Orion revision
An upgrade is a normal reviewable engineering change on a branch. Nothing is applied automatically, and semantic conflicts are resolved by people or agents under review. Tags help humans choose a known release point but do not change this workflow. Ordinary conflicts in project-modified shared files do not by themselves indicate a MAJOR Orion release.
Run `git fetch orion-upstream` and `pnpm orion:status`. Review upstream changes with `git log --oneline <baseline>..orion-upstream/main` and `git diff <baseline> orion-upstream/main`, including ADRs, policies, migrations, tooling, and `.orion/derivation.json`.
Choose the candidate commit; it must be on `orion-upstream/main`. Create a branch, for example `git switch -c orion-upgrade/<short-commit>`, and run `git merge --no-ff <commit>`.
Resolve conflicts in `.orion/project.json`, `.orion/derivation.json`, the release registry, and `package.json` first if they prevent the command from loading. Run `pnpm orion:prune` while other merge conflicts remain. It deletes foundation-only paths the merge changed or added (resolving their modify/delete conflicts), renames foundation package-scope references in resolved shared files, and stages those changes. It leaves unresolved shared files and project-owned files untouched, reports the unresolved paths, and refuses to delete a recorded durable migration or follow linked paths outside the checkout. Resolve and stage reported conflicts, then rerun it.
Resolve remaining conflicts according to [content ownership](#content-ownership): keep the project's version of project-owned files and merge shared files. Never hand-merge generated output: run the generators from step 5, then stage their results (for example `git add -A apps/web/src/generated docs/generated packages/sdk/src/generated`), which resolves conflicts in generated files, including ones the project's output no longer contains. Rerun `pnpm orion:prune` until it reports no unresolved files. Review semantic interactions with product code even where Git reports no conflict.
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm db:generate`, `pnpm -C apps/api references:write`, `pnpm -C packages/sdk generate`, `pnpm docs:references:write`, and `pnpm validate`. Commit the merge.
Run `pnpm orion:record-baseline <commit>`. It refuses unless the worktree is clean and `orion-upstream` exists and satisfies the [remote rules](#remote-rules). It then fetches `main` from that verified foundation, so refs fetched earlier from another repository cannot vouch for the commit. Finally it requires the commit to be on `orion-upstream/main`, descend from the recorded baseline, and already be an ancestor of `HEAD`. Commit the manifest change, rerun `pnpm validate`, and open the pull request against the project's `main`.
Merge the pull request with a merge commit. Squash or rebase merges discard Orion's commit identities, and `pnpm orion:check` then fails because the recorded baseline is not an ancestor of `HEAD`. The project repository must therefore keep merge commits enabled (project human action PH-02). This applies only to Orion upgrade pull requests.
If the project's default branch requires pull requests, as PH-02 establishes, the merge and baseline update reach `main` together through that pull request. Record the upgrade and any project-specific follow-up in the project plan.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Migrate a project from schema version 1
text:
Migrate a project from schema version 1
Projects initialized before the clean-baseline contract have a schema version 1 manifest with `referenceImplementations`, Orion's plan, human actions, and acceptance report, and usually the Approval Request implementation and `@orion/*` packages. After merging an Orion revision that contains this contract, `pnpm orion:check` refuses the old manifest. Migrate in the upgrade branch:
If the project adopted Approval Request as product behavior, move its code, schema, metadata, grants, and tests out of the foundation-only paths first (for example to `src/features/<product-module>/` and matching paths under the module's own name). Preserve every released migration at its original path and remove that path from the project's `foundationOnly` list in `.orion/derivation.json`; never rename or delete it. Verify uncertain release status under [migration policy](database/migrations.md) before classifying a migration as removable. Only genuinely unreleased reference migrations may be removed or renamed. `orion:prune` refuses removal of recorded durable migrations.
Edit `.orion/project.json`: set `schemaVersion` to `2`, remove `referenceImplementations`, and add `"packageScope": "@<scope>"`.
Run `pnpm orion:prune` to remove foundation-only paths and rename package-scope references.
Replace the project-owned files that still carry Orion's content: render `README.md`, `apps/api/src/modules.ts`, `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`, and the brand assets from the [templates](../.orion/derivation.json) (substituting each `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`), keeping existing project-specific text. Keep `docs/project/`; remove its references to Orion's plan, human actions, acceptance report, and reference implementation, and port the maintenance rules from the plan and human-action templates.
Regenerate as in [upgrade step 5](#upgrade-to-a-newer-orion-revision), run `pnpm validate`, and continue with baseline recording.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Contributing improvements back to Orion
text:
Contributing improvements back to Orion
Product work never goes to `orion-upstream`; its push URL is disabled. To improve the foundation itself, make the change in a separate clone of Orion and submit it there under Orion's own review, then adopt it in projects through the upgrade workflow. Do not move product code, requirements, or history into Orion. In Orion, keep new shared content independent of foundation-only content; extend `.orion/derivation.json` when adding foundation-only or project-owned files.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Limits
text:
Limits
Provenance proves which Orion commits are ancestors of the project; it does not prove that the project still follows every inherited policy. Validation and review remain the enforcement.
`pnpm orion:check` can verify that the recorded baseline is integrated, but only `pnpm orion:status` with a fetched upstream can report newer integrated commits that were not yet recorded.
Upgrades that change foundation-only or project-owned files conflict in projects; projects that diverge heavily from shared files should expect more conflicts there.
The isolation check matches links, imports, path names, and listed terms; it cannot judge whether shared prose implicitly assumes the reference implementation. Review remains necessary.
The immutable Git commit remains the exact foundation revision and provenance identity. [Foundation versioning](versioning.md) assigns human-readable tags only to deliberate stable release points; commits between tags remain usable by SHA.

title: Teluni Product Architecture
heading: Baseline and accepted architecture directions
text:
Baseline and accepted architecture directions
**Implemented foundation:** Node.js/TypeScript ESM, Fastify, PostgreSQL/Prisma infrastructure, TypeBox/OpenAPI and generated TypeScript SDK, React/Vite with TanStack Router/Query, Pino/OpenTelemetry, local validation and CI configuration. [Current product composition](README.md#verified-baseline) includes identity and the first organizations increment in the API and web application. Installed versions are owned by package manifests/lockfile. [PH-11 policies](identity-and-access.md) and accepted ADR-0024/ADR-0025 select Keycloak, server-managed sessions and application-owned scoped access. [D-01](tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status) and [D-02](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) record verified local capabilities and remaining work; real-environment provisioning is pending.
**Decided constraints:** use Orion's boundaries; keep a modular backend; support tenants from the first product slice; treat clients and uploaded files as untrusted; avoid premature microservices and distributed infrastructure.
**Accepted component direction, partially implemented:** three product components: an administration web panel, the backend, and a native Android TV player. The panel and API provide the identity/organization increments; the player remains unimplemented. The initial deployment would serve the panel/API and private media over HTTPS, with PostgreSQL and local persistent media storage on one managed host. The player downloads authorized publications and plays locally. This is a logical topology, not deployed infrastructure.

Minimum Android/API level, media profiles, persistence library, background behavior, package distribution, and update channels remain pending. No player directory or build system is created in this stage. A future repository placement should make the Android runtime independent; a conceptual name such as `apps/player-android/` is not an existing workspace package. Kotlin must not import TypeScript application internals; HTTP contracts remain interoperable.

title: Teluni Product Architecture
heading: Conceptual entities and relationships
text:
Conceptual entities and relationships
This is a domain model for review, not a database schema, migration, wire contract, or generated reference.
Entity
Relationship and invariant
Platform
Operates customer companies; platform operational authority is distinct from tenant membership
Company
Tenant ownership boundary for branches, members, media, programming, devices and publications
Branch
Belongs to one company; holds local business timezone/settings and assigned devices
User / membership / profile / grant
One stable human identity can hold independent company memberships and additive explicit branch/capability grants; temporary grants expire, suspension denies, and a designated responsible company administrator approves other administrators. Policies are selected; schema/enforcement remain proposed
Device / enrollment session
A device belongs to one company and branch after pairing; enrollment is temporary and single-use; reassignment requires safe unlink/clear semantics
Device group
Persistent company-owned programming target in the MVP; may span branches of that company within the caller's authorization. Each device belongs to zero or one programming group and follows it unless an explicit individual override replaces its complete programming
Media asset / stored object
Tenant-owned metadata points to a validated immutable file version; storage location is not authorization
Playlist / item
Company-owned ordered references to eligible media with duration semantics; edits produce draft changes
Screen composition / content area
FR-10 requires freeform configuration, independent areas with optional coordinated pages, regional schedules and concurrent video/audio. Portable representation, renderer and supported profiles remain technical work
Catalog definition / field / record / binding
FR-11 requires user-defined typed catalogs beyond products, stable/versioned field meaning and authorized data bindings. Product-price and weekly-agenda views are configurations, not a fixed universal product schema
Price override / publication intent
Designated monetary semantics permit company base/branch override and automatic publication of affected published bindings; ordinary unrelated drafts stay unpublished. Durable processing and exact price/representation contracts remain D-10/D-11
Schedule / assignment
Associates eligible programming with a device or group and local-time rule; all references share tenant and permitted branch scope
Publication / manifest
Immutable validated snapshot of programming, assets and interpretation version; references remain resolvable through retention
Device publication state
Separates desired, staged, active and last-reported versions per device; acknowledgement is not proof of continuous playback
Device report / audit event
Observation belongs to a tenant/device; attributable action evidence has independent integrity and retention requirements
Commercial period / license allocation / usage reservation
Conceptual tenant-owned trial/paid/grace boundaries, contracted independent outputs, explicit device assignment/replacement and reserved/observed usage; approval is not a payment or production quota result. Concrete schemas/state consistency remain D-12
**Initial release requirements:** [release policies](release-policies.md) define the owner-approved freeform/hybrid regional behavior and configurable catalogs, including automatic versioned price publication. [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) define the qualification envelope. [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-propose-versioned-catalog-and-composition-publications.md) establishes the accepted versioned schema/composition/publication direction alongside accepted ADR-0019. Serialization, renderer, physical storage, exact module collaboration and executable contracts are not selected or implemented by product-policy approval.
**Further evolution unless separately approved:** richer external-data widgets, managed campaign engines, ERP/POS workflows and AI authoring. Configurable fields, product presets and weekly-agenda views are already initial requirements. Versioned textual layouts and automatic price publication must preserve snapshot consistency rather than mutate live data behind an issued publication. Custom catalogs do not imply arbitrary executable plugins or direct per-customer SQL/schema administration.
Tenant IDs must participate in ownership validation for references and uniqueness. The physical enforcement choice (including compound constraints and possible row-level security) is [ADR-0018](../adr/0018-propose-tenant-owned-data-in-the-modular-backend.md): shared database/schema, explicit tenant ownership and reference constraints are accepted; concrete constraints and the additional row-level-security evaluation remain design work. IDs supplied by the caller never establish authority.

title: Teluni Product Architecture
heading: Publication and integration boundaries
text:
Publication and integration boundaries
[Playback/sync](playback-and-sync.md) owns publication consistency and recovery. Candidate HTTP operations must follow existing [API principles](../api/principles.md), [error contract](../api/error-contract.md), [API versioning](../api/versioning.md), and [delivery policy](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md). No endpoint paths, payload schemas, protocol version numbers, jobs, broker, WebSocket, S3 provider, CDN, or Kotlin client generator are selected here. Polling/reconciliation is a candidate; notification transport remains D-04.
**Future:** an externally consumable documented API should allow authorized partners to update product/price data from ERP/POS systems, with stable generated OpenAPI documentation, scoped machine identities, rate limits, versioning, and safe retry/webhook semantics. Documentation must be usable by partner companies without private repository access. The current internal living portal is not proof of a public integration service. Integrations must pass application authorization and validation; no direct ERP database coupling.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Decision scope and evidence
text:
Decision scope and evidence
**Decided for planning on 2026-10-18:** the owner explicitly approved all recommendations in the 38-question PH-12 working questionnaire and requested completion of the action. This document owns the initial commercial policy, price-validation offer, pilot/trial terms, resource-accounting direction and support/cancellation choices. Its English decision record replaces the external Portuguese working file as the canonical source.
PH-12 closes **owner commercial-policy selection**, not empirical business validation. Its original combined scope is explicitly split: **PH-18** retains customer acceptance, measured cost/support, actual support coverage and capacity-qualified offer evidence; **PH-19** retains billing-issuer/fiscal-process readiness. Neither is completed or waived. PJ-14 must collect pilot results and PJ-27 must implement/qualify the selected commercial controls before their use. This preserves the original evidence obligations without asking the owner to approve the same policy again.
**Price validation:** BRL 79.90/company/month for up to two screen licenses; BRL 29.90/month for each additional license. These are owner-approved initial validation prices, not a published offer, proven willingness to pay, profitability result or delivered entitlement. Initially offer one monthly plan in Brazil/BRL with the approved delivered product capabilities; no permanent free plan, annual offer or financial referral incentive. Public signup still requires all applicable readiness gates. No subscription, quota, payment, tax, billing issuer or commercial lifecycle implementation exists today. No paid service, customer contact, invoice, contract or public launch is authorized by this document.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Pilot and public trial
text:
Pilot and public trial
The first candidate pilot may receive **30 free software days for up to two screens**, starting only after functional setup and the operator's explicit start confirmation. Hardware, travel, installation beyond the included onboarding and content-production services are separate. Confirm participation/physical devices under PH-08, written/comparably attributable commercial agreement under PH-18 and privacy/readiness before real use. Owner approval is not customer acceptance. Extensions must be bounded, justified and recorded.
Present intended post-pilot price/conditions before starting. Conversion requires explicit commercial acceptance and the first confirmed payment; no unexpected automatic charging, silent lifetime discount or indefinite free continuation. Collect core usability, offline/recovery and device results alongside physical storage, transfer/processing, onboarding/support time, customer objections and willingness to continue. Public use of the client's name, logo, images or testimonial needs separate permission.
Public eligible verified companies receive an automatically activated **14-day trial**, starting at company activation, with a visible end instant and notices. No card is required and there is no permanent free subscription. The trial includes up to **two screens, one branch, five members and 2 GiB of original media**, plus **10 GiB of player media transfers** during the trial. Scope/abuse checks and qualified global capacity are admission prerequisites; do not substitute routine manual company approval for the PH-11 signup decision. Publish only an offer the host can actually admit safely.
At trial end, disallow new publishing, uploads and device enrollment. An authenticated, otherwise-authorized account may retain explicitly permitted contracting, account recovery and export paths in a **commercially restricted** state. This is distinct from a security-suspended account/company: commercial exceptions cannot bypass identity or security suspension. One evaluation per legitimate organization, with attributable assisted exceptions and proportionate abuse controls; email-domain/IP/name similarity alone neither proves shared ownership nor merges companies. No automatic trial extension; a justified exception must be bounded/audited.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Screen licenses and pricing
text:
Screen licenses and pricing
One screen license authorizes one player/device for one independently programmed playback output. Multiple regions, images/videos, catalog views or simultaneous functions within that output do not incur separate screen fees. The application does not claim to detect the number of physical panels attached through HDMI cloning. Multiple independent outputs need their own supported profile and explicit licensing before sale.
Customers contract a fixed license capacity per billing period. Assignment occupies a license until explicitly deallocated; connectivity/heartbeat does not create, cancel or meter the subscription. Turning off a TV does not reduce the contracted package. Separate companies do not silently share a minimum fee or discounts.
For the initial validation offer, one or two screens cost the BRL 79.90 company minimum. For `n > 2`, the proposed monthly total is BRL 79.90 + BRL 29.90 × (`n` − 2). Example totals: three screens BRL 109.80, four BRL 139.70 and ten BRL 319.10. Automatic table-based offers stop at ten licenses initially; larger fleets need a capacity/cost-qualified quote, without an automatic volume discount. Ten is an offer boundary, not a platform architecture limit; the reference 100-player benchmark is not measured host capacity.
Replace a failed player through an explicit license transfer and revocation, without an extra replacement charge. An unreachable old player may retain its already-issued authorization until expiry, at most seven days. Allow one pending replacement per license, report any overlap and prevent repeated replacement rotation; this is an explicit recovery exception, not an unlimited extra license. Cross-company reassignment still needs verified wipe/reset under the release security policy.
The single initial plan includes the approved capabilities that have actually been delivered. Never sell roadmap features as available. Do not gate HTTPS, isolation, required MFA, recovery, security fixes or reliable offline operation as paid upgrades. Do not separately charge per member/branch or per simultaneous screen function initially; explicit qualified technical limits still apply to members, branches, records, fields, layouts and imports. "No per-user fee" does not mean infinite resources. Trial-specific limits remain distinct.

Account for actual transmitted media bytes, including retransmissions. Internal failure retries must not silently double-charge processing. Protect sufficient physical capacity for renditions, history, current/recovery/staging generations, deduplicated references and backups; do not present the customer's original-media quota as total host disk demand. License/plan increases require explicit confirmation and a demonstrated prorated charge for the remaining cycle; reductions take effect at renewal, with explicit choice of licenses to deactivate. Specify exact monetary rounding/calendar rules in the reviewed future contract. Warn about usage over the intended lower quota and resolve it before confirming reduction; never erase protected data or choose arbitrary TVs to make a downgrade fit.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Hardware, onboarding and support
text:
Hardware, onboarding and support
Customers initially supply compatible displays/players, power and network. Teluni must qualify the devices it advertises under PH-08 and diagnose its software faults; do not promise all Smart TVs are supported. Hardware resale/lease is not selected.
Include one remote onboarding/training session up to **60 minutes**. Quote onsite work, travel, physical installation, network/electrical services and extraordinary setup separately before acceptance; any first-pilot concession must be explicit. Include delivered tools/templates and usage guidance, not recurring artwork, catalog entry, campaign production or outsourced daily content operation. Paid AI and unlimited human work are not included by implication. Record the cost of included onboarding too.
P23/P24 were conditional recommendations. **Email/form are the baseline record channels; WhatsApp is optional only after actual coverage is confirmed.** No phone number/address/account is invented. Actual operator availability, support window and calendar remain **unknown under PH-18**, rather than asserting a 09:00–18:00 or 24/7 commitment. Use explicitly arranged pilot support while coverage is being established; before any public support offer, publish only the verified window and confront it with restaurant evening/weekend needs.
The selected target is a **useful first response within one business day of the established coverage calendar**, not an automated receipt or fixed resolution deadline. It cannot be advertised as an unconditional service commitment before that coverage is verified. Prioritize critical incidents and communicate according to real coverage; no formal availability/resolution SLA is sold at this stage. Repeated support demand calls for product improvements, training or offer review, not an arbitrary bug-support cutoff. Content access continues to require PH-11 scoped consent, expiry and the support person's real identity.
Explain residential power/network limitations, maintenance and incident communication before the pilot. Normal playback can continue from a valid local generation, but login, publishing, recovery and current diagnostics still depend on services/network. Formal SLA offers require measured compatible infrastructure and support; internal targets are not a commercial guarantee.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Payment, expiry, cancellation and retention
text:
Payment, expiry, cancellation and retention
Start with **monthly prepayment**, explicit billing dates/license quantity and **Pix/bank transfer with attributable manual reconciliation**. A screenshot alone does not prove settled payment. Only an explicitly authorized platform billing operator may confirm settlement or change commercial grants; company administrators may request/manage their own contracted capacity/cancellation without marking themselves paid. Concrete capabilities remain D-12 review, not implemented role identifiers. No bank destination, payment-provider integration, tax treatment or fiscal issuer is selected here. PH-19 must establish the appropriate billing/fiscal process before charging. Gateway/card automation remains future; basic commercial authorization cannot be deferred just because invoicing is manual.
Late-payment policy: notices and **seven days of commercial grace after the due date**. Thereafter deny new publications/enrollment and new commercial playback renewals, while allowing only explicitly authorized regularization/recovery/export paths for otherwise valid accounts. Maintain the security-suspension distinction. Do not invent penalties/interest or silent billable continuation; final conditions require review before contracting.
For trial, paid-period expiry/cancellation and applicable grace, future player authorization must be bounded by **both** the known commercial playback deadline and the maximum seven-day offline renewal interval. The shorter bound wins. Do not retroactively claim that an unreachable device received a newly shortened deadline, instantly stopped or erased its cache. Existing valid leases may survive an unreachable revocation until their previously issued deadline. On reconnect, reconcile current payment/authorization and content validity; no reset of an expired commercial period or bypass through old snapshots. These are required behaviors to qualify, not an implemented credential format.
Offer simple monthly cancellation without a minimum-stay penalty for future renewals; normally retain the already-paid period to its end, subject to legitimate security controls. Show the effective date/license impact and export path. Refunds, exceptions and applicable rights belong to transparent reviewed terms, not a fabricated legal conclusion or waiver. No annual prepayment/discount is offered initially. Do not silently stack pilot, volume or referral discounts.
Select a **30-day product window for authorized reactivation/export** after commercial end, without edit/publication. This is not a promise to erase every byte on day 31. Reconcile PH-13 personal-data/audit/backup obligations, the at-least-90-day publication-history target and protected active/staging/recovery references. Distinguish limited account access, physical deletion and offline cache erasure. Measure the cost of closed-trial retention and stop new admission when safe capacity is unavailable.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Economics, market and readiness
text:
Economics, market and readiness
Initial market is **Brazil/BRL**, with internationalization retained and no silent currency conversion. Foreign sales, annual plans, automated billing, recurring commissions and financial referral rewards require later evaluation. Record partner interest without a current incentive; referrals grant no access to customer data or shared human credentials.
No new recurring procurement is authorized now. With received revenue or a demonstrated operating need, prepare a total-cost budget and a separately approved procurement/migration proposal. Residential hosting, backup, identity and reliable email requirements are not waived by zero procurement budget; unresolved readiness prevents operation/admission. Revenue alone neither proves capacity nor authorizes spending.
Use an **at least 70% steady-state contribution-margin target** as an owner-approved validation goal. For this exercise, deduct applicable taxes/fees and attributable variable costs including valued recurring support; keep onboarding, fixed costs and investment recovery separately visible and do not double-count them. Value the owner's time initially at **BRL 50/hour as a stated analytical assumption**, not measured salary or an external-service price. Fixed costs belong in break-even analysis; cash increment, economic allocation and sunk investment are distinct.
At BRL 79.90 and a 70% target, the deductible-cost budget would be BRL 23.97/month/company. This is arithmetic, not a measured cost or proven profit. The pilot must determine whether actual taxes, transfer/processing, support and other attributable costs fit; revise price/offer before expanding if they do not. Unknown taxes or own labor are never zero by default. Qualified fiscal/legal review precedes charging/public terms; source Apache-2.0 licensing does not replace SaaS terms or fiscal documentation.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for the server side of D-03, 2026-10-19.** The owner approved all nine [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed under [PH-22](human-actions.md#ph-22), including ADR-0027, and asked for implementation in [PJ-08](implementation-plan.md#current-work). Approval authorizes implementation in local and CI environments with simulated players; [implementation status](#implementation-status) records what exists.
In scope: the device identity and its company/branch assignment, temporary-code enrollment, the device credential and how the API authenticates it, reported capabilities and the configured rotation (FR-03), the server's offline authorization deadline (AT-15), renaming, moving between branches, unlinking, erasure confirmation and reassignment (FR-02, P24), permissions, abuse limits, audit, data, contracts, panel workflow and verification.
Out of scope, with their owners: the Android application and its secure local storage, clock estimation and enforcement of the deadline on the device (D-07, PJ-12); signed authorization envelopes, manifests and synchronization (D-04, PJ-11); content assignment to devices and groups (PJ-10); trial, license and quota admission for enrollment (PJ-27); qualifying any hardware or orientation profile (PH-08). The design leaves explicit hooks for each and claims none of them.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Pairing codes are temporary, single-use, bound to the requesting device, rate-limited and safe under concurrent claims; the claiming person must already be authorized for the destination company and branch; a displayed code is not an enduring credential ([security requirements](security-and-i18n.md#pairing-and-device-lifecycle), FR-02).
Pairing, moving, unlinking and resetting devices is company-wide for administrators and limited to authorized source and destination branches for branch managers; operators need an additional grant ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). Administrator and branch-manager grants count only in strongly authenticated sessions (P12).
Offline authorization expires no later than seven days after its last successful online renewal (AT-15, P22); commercial deadlines may shorten it (PJ-27).
Unlink needs explicit authorized confirmation, server revocation and a distinct pending-erasure state; private content, configuration and credentials are cleared on reconnection; reassignment to another company requires verified cleanup or a controlled reset; revoked access, unreachable device and confirmed erasure stay distinct (P24).
Player identities are separate from human identities and restricted to their own assignment, media and reports. Raw codes, credentials and credential-bearing links never reach logs, errors, screenshots or support bundles. No custom cryptography or token scheme.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Mechanism overview
text:
Mechanism overview
The flow follows the shape of the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant ([RFC 8628](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628)): a device without a keyboard shows a short code, and a person who is already signed in elsewhere enters it. Teluni does not route devices through Keycloak, because devices are not human principals and Keycloak holds only human identities (ADR-0024); the API module plays both the authorization-server and resource-server role for devices.
Player                                API (devices module)                    Panel (signed-in person)
  │ generate 256-bit credential C            │                                      │
  │ POST /device-enrollments              │                                      │
  │   { credentialHash: SHA-256(C), report } │                                      │
  │ ◀── { enrollmentId, userCode, expiresAt, pollInterval }                         │
  │ show userCode on screen                  │                                      │
  │                                          │ ◀── POST /companies/{id}/devices  │
  │                                          │      { userCode, name, branch, rotation }
  │                                          │ claim: PENDING → CLAIMED, insert device
  │ POST /device-enrollments/{id}/status  │                                      │
  │   Authorization: Bearer C                │                                      │
  │ ◀── { status: "paired", deviceId }       │                                      │
  │ GET /device/self (Bearer C)  ────────▶│ configuration + authorizedUntil       │

The device generates its own credential and sends only its hash when enrollment starts. The credential itself never leaves the device until it is used, the server never returns a secret, and a lost response at any step is retried without issuing anything new. This is the central choice in [ADR-0027](../adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md).

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Enrollment
text:
Enrollment
**Start.** `POST /device-enrollments` is anonymous. The body carries the credential hash (32 bytes, base64url) and the device report (see [capabilities](#capabilities-and-rotation)). The server creates a `PENDING` enrollment valid for 10 minutes and answers with the enrollment ID, the user code, the expiry and a 5-second polling interval. A hash that already belongs to a device or any enrollment is refused with `ENROLLMENT_REJECTED`, so one credential can never bind two identities.
**User code.** Eight characters from the 20-consonant alphabet `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ`, shown as `XXXX-XXXX`, as RFC 8628 section 6.1 recommends: about 34.5 bits, no vowels (no accidental words) and no look-alike digits. Entry ignores case, spaces and hyphens. The server stores an HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalized code under a dedicated `RESTRICTED` key ring (key ID stored with the value, newest key first), never the code, so a database copy does not let anyone enumerate live codes offline. A unique index on the HMAC prevents two live enrollments from sharing a code; a collision on insert is retried with a new code.
**Claim.** In the panel, a person enters the code with a name, a destination branch and a rotation. In one transaction the server locks the company row (tenant data design rule 5), rebuilds the actor's access and requires `devices.manage` on the destination branch and an active company and branch, then moves the enrollment from `PENDING` to `CLAIMED` with a conditional update (`WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND expires_at > now()`), inserts the device with the enrollment's credential hash and report, and writes one `device.paired` audit event. Exactly one of two concurrent claims succeeds; the other, an expired code, a used code and an unknown code all answer the same `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID`, so the answer does not reveal which case applied. The rotation must be one the device reported as supported.
**Status.** The device polls `POST /device-enrollments/{id}/status` with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`; the server checks the credential against the enrollment's hash. Answers are `pending` (with the polling interval), `paired` (with the device ID) or `expired`. Polling faster than the interval answers `RATE_LIMITED` with the interval to use. Pending enrollments expire lazily: reads treat an expired row as expired and a purge deletes `PENDING` rows one day after expiry, and `CLAIMED` rows 30 days after the claim.
**Commercial hook.** The claim transaction is where PJ-27 will add trial, license and quota admission. Until then only company and branch status gate enrollment.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Device credential and authentication
text:
Device credential and authentication
**Credential.** 32 bytes from the platform CSPRNG, generated and kept by the player in Android Keystore-backed storage (D-07, PJ-12). The server stores only its SHA-256 under a unique index; because the credential has 256 bits of entropy, an unkeyed hash is sufficient for lookup and gives nothing usable from a database copy. The credential is `RESTRICTED`: never in logs, telemetry, errors, audit, query strings or the panel.
**Use.** Device operations declare a new operation access kind, `device`, and expect `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` on paths under `/device/`. The devices module resolves the credential to the device on every request, with no cache, so revocation takes effect on the next request. Device routes never accept the human session cookie, and human routes never accept a device credential. The shared runtime gains only the access kind; the devices module owns the lookup.
**States.** An `ACTIVE` device's credential reaches every device operation. A `REVOKED` device's credential reaches only `GET /device/self`, which answers `{ status: "unlinked", clearRequired: true }`, and `POST /device/self/erasure`, which confirms clearing. Any other credential answers `DEVICE_UNAUTHORIZED` with no detail.
**Rotation.** `POST /device/self/credential` replaces the hash with a new device-generated one. The previous hash stays valid until the new credential is first used, so a lost response leaves the device with a working credential. Rotation is in the last delivery increment; it is not required by the first player.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Check-in and the offline authorization deadline
text:
Check-in and the offline authorization deadline
`GET /device/self` returns the device's ID, name, branch name and time zone, rotation, status and `authorizedUntil`. For an active device, `authorizedUntil` is the database clock plus seven days (AT-15), later capped by a commercial deadline under PJ-27. `PUT /device/self/report` updates the reported capabilities. Each successful device request updates `last_seen_at`, written at most once per minute per device so check-ins do not cause a write per request.
In this design `authorizedUntil` is a server statement in an authenticated HTTPS response. Making it tamper-evident on the device (a signed envelope) and enforcing it against a trusted local clock (AT-16) belong to D-04/PJ-11 and D-07/PJ-12. The panel shows "last seen" and, for unreachable devices, the latest deadline the device could hold, so operators never read server intent as device state.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Capabilities and rotation
text:
Capabilities and rotation
The device report is bounded, validated JSON: application version, protocol version, manufacturer and model (each at most 80 characters), Android version, display width and height in pixels (1 to 16384) and the supported rotations. It is stored as reported and labelled "reported by the device" in the panel; it is not a qualified hardware profile (PH-08), and nothing in this design claims support for a device because it reported a capability.
The configured orientation is a rotation of 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise: 0 and 180 are horizontal, 90 and 270 vertical (FR-03). A rotation, rather than a horizontal/vertical flag, tells the player which way the screen is physically mounted. Setting a rotation the device did not report as supported answers `ROTATION_UNSUPPORTED`; the panel offers only reported rotations.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Device lifecycle
text:
Device lifecycle
          claim                       unlink                       device confirms clearing
(none) ─────────▶ ACTIVE ───────────────────────────▶ REVOKED, erasure PENDING ───────────▶ REVOKED, erasure CONFIRMED
                  │  rename, set rotation, move           │ record controlled reset (person)
                  │  (same company only)                  └──────────────────────────────▶ REVOKED, erasure RESET_RECORDED

**Rename and rotation.** Need `devices.manage` on the device's branch and the expected version.
**Move.** Changes the branch within the same company. Needs `devices.manage` on both the source and the destination branch, an active destination branch and the expected version. Moving to another company is not an operation: it is an unlink followed by a new enrollment.
**Unlink.** Needs `devices.manage` on the device's branch, the expected version and an explicit confirmation in the panel that names the device. It sets `REVOKED` with erasure `PENDING` in one transaction; from then on the credential reaches only the two operations above. It cannot be undone; the device is paired again with a new enrollment.
**Erasure confirmation.** When an unlinked device reconnects, it learns `clearRequired`, deletes private content, configuration and its credential locally (PJ-12), and only then calls `POST /device/self/erasure` with the credential it is about to discard. The server records `CONFIRMED`, deletes the credential hash and writes `device.erasure_confirmed`. If the response is lost, the device has already cleared and the record stays `PENDING`, shown honestly as unconfirmed, which is the safe direction.
**Controlled reset.** A device that will never reconnect (factory reset, broken, lost) stays `PENDING`. A person with `devices.manage` can record that the device was reset locally; the record says `RESET_RECORDED` with the actor, not `CONFIRMED`, and audit keeps the difference.
**Reassignment.** The server cannot recognize a physical device across identities, so verified cleanup is enforced where it can be: the player starts a new enrollment only from a state with no credential and no private content, and when it still holds a credential it first completes the erasure confirmation above. A new enrollment always creates a new device identity; the old record keeps its own history. The panel lists unlinked devices with their erasure state until the purge below.
Archived branches keep their devices; archiving a branch that still has active devices answers `BRANCH_IN_USE`, through a guard the devices module registers on the organizations access port, so a device is never left in a branch nobody can manage.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Permissions
text:
Permissions
Two capabilities are added to the organizations domain, which owns role presets:
Capability
Company administrator
Branch manager
Operator
`devices.view`: list devices, see details and state
Company
Granted branches
Granted branches
`devices.manage`: pair, rename, set rotation, move, unlink, record reset
Company
Granted branches (source and destination for a move)
No (needs an additional grant; custom profiles are PJ-24)
Hidden devices answer `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Every operation resolves access on the request through the organizations public port and never takes company, branch or role from the request body as authority.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
Proposed initial values:
Enrollment start: the existing per-route rate limit plus at most 20 starts per client address per hour, and at most 10,000 pending enrollments platform-wide, after which starts answer `RATE_LIMITED`. A full pending table makes a guessed code at most 10,000 in 2.56 × 10¹⁰ likely to match.
Claim: at most 10 failed claims per person per 15 minutes and 30 per company per 15 minutes, counted in PostgreSQL from failed-claim rows that record only the actor, company and time. Exceeding a limit answers `RATE_LIMITED` without saying which applied. With these limits an attacker with one account needs on the order of years of attempts per expected match against a full pending table. Many accounts or companies created for guessing remain a residual risk that the signup abuse controls (PH-13) must bound; a successful guess pairs a stranger's screen to the attacker's company, which its owner notices because pairing fails on their side, and no tenant data is exposed.
Status polling: once per polling interval per enrollment.
The per-address limit uses the address Fastify reports for the connection, as the identity routes do; behind a reverse proxy it counts the proxy until trusted forwarding is configured for the production deployment.
These limits stand on their own; commercial device quotas are PJ-27.
